title: Digital Room stage directive
description: Attached by the Cognigy agent to a message as data._showroom. Instructs the frontend stage what to render. The frontend is a thin renderer: it must not infer anything not present here.

v.description: Contract version. Bump only on a breaking change; the frontend must ignore directives with an unknown version rather than guessing.

action.description: show = render asset without autoplay. play = render and start. seek = jump within the current asset. highlight = draw attention to a region of the current asset. step = advance a walkthrough or tour. clear = empty the stage. offer = carry quick-reply buttons and change nothing on the stage; it exists because cta is applied independently of the action while every other action has a side effect, so offering a choice would otherwise disturb what the visitor is looking at. wrapup = replace the stage with the closing summary; the chat stays open and the visitor can carry on, which is why it does not end the session.

summary.description: Required for action=wrapup. The closing summary, built from what the visitor ACTUALLY viewed rather than from the model's recollection of the conversation.

headline.description: Short closing line, usually including their first name.

crm.description: Whether NiCE already has a relationship with this company, so the closing page can name the person who owns it instead of offering a generic form. Omit entirely when no lookup happened, which is the case for a NiCE employee browsing for their own knowledge. The panel must render correctly without it.

status.description: known means a record was found and someone owns the relationship. new-lead means nothing matched, which is the common case and is a finding, not a failure.

salesRepName.description: Only meaningful when status is known: a new lead has nobody assigned yet, which is the whole point of the distinction. This names a real employee to an unauthenticated visitor, so see the disclosure gate in docs/solution-design.md before it carries real data.

accountName.description: The account as CRM holds it, which may differ from what the visitor typed.

matchType.description: Which record matched. Carried so the closing line can be honest about the strength of the relationship rather than treating a stale lead like an active opportunity.

viewed.description: Assets actually put on the stage this session, in order, deduplicated.

watchUrl.description: Present only where the asset has a genuinely public address.

topics.description: Candidate topics to explore further, offered as checkboxes. Derived from the use cases and products of what they viewed, plus what they said they were interested in.

preselected.description: True for topics drawn from what they actually watched, as opposed to adjacent suggestions.

emailKnown.description: Whether an email address was captured during the introduction. The panel must NOT assume permission to use it: having an address is not consent to be contacted, so the follow-up offer is an explicit opt-in.

asset.description: Required for show and play. Omitted for control actions on the already-loaded asset.

type.description: embed is a third-party player rendered in an iframe, currently YouTube. It differs from video in two ways that matter: position is applied as a start offset when the frame loads rather than as a live seek, and the host page cannot read playback state, so chapter narration does not fire.

summary.description: One or two sentences describing the asset, displayed on the stage. Used by document assets, where the visitor is deciding whether the thing is worth opening and the title alone does not tell them. Carried from the catalog, never written by the agent, so what is shown on the stage is the publisher's own description.

badges.description: Short factual labels shown next to a document, for example its content type and industries. Every value must come from the publisher's own taxonomy: these read as statements of fact about the resource, so an inferred value does not belong here. Deliberately one generic list rather than separate contentType and industries fields, because the renderer only lays them out, and two fields it treats identically would be a permanent contract obligation with no behaviour behind it.

src.description: Resolved playable or renderable URL. Resolved by the backend, never assembled by the agent.

chapters.description: Video chapters. talkTrack is spoken by the agent in the chat rail as the chapter plays.

steps.description: Walkthrough steps for type=walkthrough. Each step is a screenshot plus an optional hotspot.

hotspot.description: Region to highlight, as fractions of image width and height (0 to 1).

position.description: Target time in seconds for action=seek. Zero-based index for action=step. On show and play it is an optional START OFFSET, which lets the agent open a video at a chapter in a single directive rather than a play-then-seek pair.

tour.description: Present when the visitor is inside a guided tour, so the stage can render progress.

cta.description:
Suggested next actions rendered as buttons. Selecting one sends its value back to the agent as user input.

Keep it to three or four for a conversational follow-up: more than that stops reading as a suggestion and starts reading as a form. The higher limit exists for the one case that is genuinely a closed list rather than a suggestion, the twelve industries in catalog/industries.json, where any shortlist would be us guessing which vertical the visitor is in.

value.description: Text sent back to the agent when selected.
